title: Post-incident instrumentation: tracing & metrics gaps for capacity regression
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: During a capacity regression on 2026-03-09 we observed elevated end-to-end latencies and a large number of queued requests that caused tail latency violations for Hosted API customers. The incident postmortem identified several observability blind spots in the Console/observability surface that impeded diagnosis and prolonged mitigation: missing per-route p95 by model variant, no KV cache hit-rate metric surfaced to the console, dashboards aggregated away burst queue length spikes, and trace spans were not instrumented to correlate request_id -> GPU job_id. This ticket tracks remediation work to close those gaps and validate coverage via synthetic tests and runbooks.

Details & impact: The regression was triggered by a serving runtime change that increased transient queueing in the request router under load. Engineers could see aggregate token/sec and node-level GPU metrics, but not: (1) route-level inflight queue length (per-tenant, per-model), (2) KV cache hit/miss rate over time with percentiles, (3) tracing link between incoming request trace_id and internal gpu_job_id, (4) per-model-variant p95 latency broken down by deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private). The lack of these signals slowed root cause confirmation by ~2 hours and prevented targeted canary rollbacks for a subset of customers.

Root cause (observability-specific): Instrumentation selectors in the router were filtering tags to reduce cardinality; as a result customer_id and model_variant tags were dropped from queueing and KV cache metrics. Tracing library upgrade removed an internal span hook that attached gpu_job_id to the root trace for high-throughput paths. Dashboard construction used 1-minute rollups that hid 15–30s burst spikes.

Objectives: 1) restore and add the missing metrics and trace tags without unbounded cardinality growth; 2) update console dashboards to surface short-lived queue spikes and model-variant p95; 3) add synthetic monitors and playbook checks to detect regressions earlier; 4) validate with load tests and a post-deploy smoke run before the next runtime release.
action_items: A1. Add 'model_variant' and 'deployment_mode' tags to router queue metrics and emit p95/p99 for per-route latency. Owner: Marco Chen. Due: 2026-03-18.
A2. Add KV cache hit/miss counters and percentiles, include a computed hit-rate time-series and a high-cardinality-but-sampled tag for customer_id. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-19.
A3. Re-add gpu_job_id to tracing spans for hot paths via a lightweight span-attachment hook; ensure spans propagate across async worker boundary. Owner: Diego Alvarez. Due: 2026-03-15.

A4. Create new dashboard panels: (a) per-route inflight queue length (5s resolution), (b) per-model-variant p95 latency (1s resolution downsampled to 5s for dashboard), (c) KV cache hit-rate heatmap. Owner: Console UX (Marta Lind). Due: 2026-03-20.
A5. Implement a synthetic monitor that replays a representative prompt mix against a canary pool and asserts p95 latency and queue length thresholds. Owner: SRE (Jordan Blake). Due: 2026-03-22.

A6. Update incident runbook with steps to query new metrics and tracing correlations, add checklist items for targeted rollback when model-variant p95 deviates >20% from baseline. Owner: Oncall Lead (Riley O'Connor). Due: 2026-03-17.
A7. Backfill short-term dashboards for the last 48h using event logs so we can validate that instrumentation would have shown the regression. Owner: Observability Data (Han Park). Due: 2026-03-16.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Per-route p95 and per-model-variant p95 are visible in Console dashboards and queries return results for a 1-hour test window. 2) KV cache hit-rate series exists and shows >0% differences when KV behavior is toggled in a load test. 3) A sample trace can be looked up by request_id and shows gpu_job_id attached for hot-path traces. 4) Synthetic monitor fires an alert in staging for an induced 25% p95 regression. 5) Updated runbook exists and is referenced in the postmortem doc.
